items.title: CV-001 is explicitly residual lineage, not product coverage
items.statement: The unit cleanly prevents residual token-bank fragments from overriding atomized contracts or being treated as implementation-ready behavior.
items.impact: Prevents stale lineage vocabulary from silently becoming runtime authority.

evidence.exact_quote: Contracts_V0-S0001 preserves source-lineage fragments only; canonical product behavior lives in CV-002 through CV-278 or referenced owner docs.

items.title: Concern identity and lifecycle remain field names rather than a closed schema
items.statement: CV-279 names concern identity, lifecycle, approval, blocked-episode, and approver concepts but does not define types, requiredness, uniqueness, referential integrity, or a legal lifecycle transition matrix. The acceptance statement that TODO prose must compile into contract-level fields is therefore not independently falsifiable from this unit.
items.impact: Consumers can serialize incompatible concern records or disagree on whether a transition and approval scope are valid.

evidence.exact_quote: Contracts_V0 owns durable concern identity, concern lifecycle fields, route/open primitives, approval_scope_key, blocked episode identity, approver identity fields, and promotion-class contract boundaries. TODO-style owner sections such as Define concern_id/project_id/run and scope refs must compile into contract-level fields or explicit source-lineage dispositions; they must not remain imperative instructions masquerading as contract prose.

items.title: Concern merge, split, and supersession authority is deliberately withheld
items.statement: CV-280 clearly permits display and routing of retained lineage while forbidding consumers from inventing executable merge, split, or supersession mutations.
items.impact: Avoids accidental mutation authority in Orchestrator and Run Graph consumers.

evidence.exact_quote: Concern merge, split, and supersession are explicit future/out-of-scope runtime mutation authority for the current implementation-readiness packet. Active concern lifecycle may display and route retained lineage ids using already registered concern identity, routing, and history fields, but executable merge/split/supersession mutations require a later dedicated contract/event registration.

items.title: Unsupported concern mutation requests lack typed failure behavior
items.statement: Although mutation authority is correctly deferred, CV-280 does not define the rejection result, allowed action set, audit receipt, or GUI behavior when a caller nevertheless requests merge, split, or supersession.
items.impact: Callers may hide, disable, or fail the same unsupported operation inconsistently and may mislead users about whether history changed.

evidence.exact_quote: Consumers may display and link lineage but cannot mutate concern history without a later contract-level event definition.

items.title: Runtime identity envelope has no concrete profile or identity invariants
items.statement: CV-281 enumerates identity domains but leaves field types, cardinality, immutability, tenant uniqueness, inheritance precedence, and the actual required/optional/inherited/forbidden matrix to future domain profiles.
items.impact: Records can pass owner-local checks while binding the wrong account, attempt, worktree, or effective identity.

evidence.exact_quote: Runtime-facing records must carry a shared runtime identity envelope with stable ids for project, run, node, attempt, package, seam, lane, worktree, actor, account, provider, requested identity, effective identity, execution_role, and subordinate provider-native correlation refs. Domain profiles may narrow required fields for permissions, providers, artifacts, routes, plan graph, and continuity records, but they must not replace the shared envelope with owner-local identity names.

items.title: Continuity contract is an obligation list, not an executable event/storage contract
items.statement: CV-282 requires a versioned schema, event family, storage keys, triggers, retention, replay, redaction, staleness, and conflict handling but supplies none of the concrete event names, key shapes, transition rules, conflict algorithm, retention periods, or deletion propagation.
items.impact: Cross-run continuity producers and consumers can implement incompatible replay, retention, and privacy behavior while claiming compliance.

evidence.exact_quote: Cross-run knowledge continuity must be represented by a versioned runtime continuity contract with schema, event family, storage keys, extraction trigger/source rules, actor/runtime_identity, project/run/account scope, retention and redaction policy, provenance/evidence refs, reconnect and replay behavior, conflict/staleness handling, and canonical runtime storage over stored outputs and handoff records. `.puppet-master/memory` is not an active storage target for this contract.

items.title: Shared route object lacks a closed wire shape and restore safety rules
items.statement: CV-283 names route-object concerns but does not define schema version negotiation, target-type enums, required identity combinations, serialization limits, fallback codes, authorization revalidation on restore, redirect-loop bounds, or back-stack conflict behavior.
items.impact: Deep links can deserialize differently across surfaces, expose stale or unauthorized targets, or loop during fallback and restore.

Route objects carry route object identity, source surface, destination surface, target object type, target identity fields, project/run/package/seam/lane/worktree/account scope, mode/context parameters, actor/runtime_identity, permission/visibility boundary, serialization format, validation/fallback behavior, stale or missing-target handling, restore/back-stack semantics, and compatibility with chain wizard routing.

items.title: Plan graph identity context is not materialized as a falsifiable schema contract
items.statement: CV-284 says two schemas must add a required identity context, but the unit does not define the object properties, requiredness by node kind, field formats, migration defaults, or validation of promotion and recovery provenance.
items.impact: Graph consumers may continue inferring identity from node ids or adopt mutually incompatible schema additions.

items.title: Same-file runtime contract precedence is explicit
items.statement: CV-285 prevents chronological addendum order from acting as implicit precedence and marks earlier short enum/event tables as compatibility lineage when named canonical units exist.
items.impact: Reduces drift between blocked payload, scheduler event, and action-id consumers.

items.statement: CV-286 assigns shared names to Contracts_V0 while retaining behavior in Goal_Runtime_System, persistence in storage-plan, and approval scope in Permissions_System; it also correctly defers concrete event registration to CV-287.

items.title: Goal event registry lacks ordering, transition, and duplicate-conflict semantics

items.title: CV-290 protects immutable approval and honest pre-activation GUI state
items.statement: The unit requires immutable Approved PRD Packs, atomic approval/outbox persistence, deterministic duplicate handling, and forbids showing a build as running or WorkNodes as runnable before activation commit and a durable start receipt.

items.title: Atomic activation state list lacks crash, cancellation, and commit-boundary semantics
items.statement: CV-290 lists activation_pending, records_materialized, entrypoints_queued, start_event_pending, active, and cancelled_before_mutation but does not define the legal transition graph, transaction participants, durable boundary for mutation beginning, queue rollback, or recovery when cancellation races a queued entrypoint or outbox delivery.

items.title: Planning topic graph mutations lack concurrency and revision control
items.statement: CV-290 authorizes add, split, merge, rename, defer, reopen, reorder, and impact propagation but does not specify PlanningRun revision/CAS, merge-conflict behavior, deterministic dependency traversal, cycle detection, or lost-update recovery for concurrent controller/user edits.
items.impact: Topic drafts can remain falsely ready, invalidations can be lost, or two edits can create divergent topic identities and dependencies.

items.title: Testing overrides and incomplete-item approvals have no enforcement lifecycle
items.statement: The unit scopes testing_policy_override and user_approved_incomplete_item records, but it does not define who reevaluates reopen or expiration conditions, how revocation propagates to affected work, or which state wins when a policy override conflicts with a required certification gate.
items.impact: Expired or revoked exceptions may continue suppressing tests or leave work displayed as acceptable indefinitely.

evidence.exact_quote: Disabling or restricting automated testing requires a durable testing_policy_override explicitly approved by the user for exact projects, PlanUnits, WorkNodes, capability classes, reasons, risks, and reopen conditions.

items.title: Discovery receipt events omit a durable event envelope and per-event requirements
items.statement: CV-291 has rich enum registries and privacy-aware payload fields, but receipt events lack schema version, event id, occurred/observed timestamps, correlation/causation, idempotency, ordering, and event-specific required/forbidden field rules.
items.impact: Discovery replay and support telemetry cannot reliably distinguish duplicate, reordered, or partially emitted invoked, selected, fallback, and verified events.

Receipt payloads preserve request_id, consumer_id, project/worktree or remote identity, query_digest, visible post-policy candidate_count, opaque/redaction-profiled selected_result_ids, freshness_state, fallback_state, policy_decision, source_index_generation, cache/ranking/policy/ignore/identity versions when cached, permission_snapshot_id, approval_scope_key, redaction_profile, SSH host trust fields when applicable, budget_ms, elapsed_ms, error_code, and verification_receipt_ref when available.

items.statement: CV-291 separates discovery-local target_kind from route_target.target_kind, limits counts to post-policy visibility, uses opaque selected-result ids, and forbids SSH secret material.
items.impact: Reduces policy-count and path disclosure while preventing enum collision with navigation contracts.

items.title: History projection is explicitly non-authoritative and rebuildable
items.statement: CV-295 consistently preserves immutable source identity, prevents projection mutation of historical truth, and requires stale/corrupt projection state to be surfaced and rebuildable.

evidence.exact_quote: History row, compare, export, open, reopen, send-forward, resume, retry, clone, rebuild, artifact, and evidence flows use identity-native refs such as artifact_id, run_id, thread_id, attempt_id, PlanningRun or pack identity, receipt refs, source record refs, manifest refs, archive state, and current-project scope. The History projection carries action availability and stale/degraded state but never becomes authority for immutable source records.

items.title: Vision bridge preserves lineage and prevents raw-image leakage to non-vision models
items.statement: CV-296 binds derived output to source image hash/ref and provider identity, carries uncertainty and redaction notes, and explicitly limits non-vision consumers to structured derived text plus source refs.
items.impact: Supports auditability, cost attribution, and least-disclosure routing.

Non-vision models consume the structured derived result and source refs, not raw image bytes.

items.title: Vision bridge result lacks durable identity, cache key, consent, and deletion semantics
items.statement: The record has no result id, schema version, generation timestamp, canonical cache-key algorithm, required usage attribution, retention policy, consent/permission snapshot identity, or cascade behavior when the source image or authorization is revoked or deleted.

items.title: OCR and derived vision text are not classified as untrusted prompt input
items.statement: CV-296 requires notable OCR and allows derived text to enter non-vision model context, but it does not require prompt-injection labeling, quoting/isolation, instruction stripping, provenance-preserving boundaries, or a policy for adversarial text embedded in images.
items.impact: An image can smuggle instructions into a downstream model despite raw-image disclosure controls.

Non-vision models consume the structured derived result and source refs, not raw image bytes.

items.title: Notification payload privacy and predicate execution boundaries are strong
items.statement: CV-298 excludes high-risk raw content and secrets, uses secret references, bounds generic webhook predicates to a small declarative atom set, and forbids scripts, shell, arbitrary JavaScript, loops, network calls, and catastrophic regex.

items.impact: A privileged or destructive command can be replayed against a reassigned host, outlive its approval, or execute without a deterministically matched receipt.

evidence.exact_quote: HostCapabilityCommand is the PM-owned command envelope for containerized hosts. It carries command_id, command_kind, host_capability_ref, host_profile_id, optional host instance/runtime ids as backend facts, execution_unit_context, approval_scope_key, permission_snapshot_id, FileSafe scope, network_access_policy, secret_access_policy, destructive_command_policy, transcript policy, cleanup policy, and required receipt refs. HostOperationRequest may remain the dispatch/request payload produced from this envelope.

items.title: Onboarding setup state is incorrectly classified gui_related false
items.statement: CV-305 defines user-visible Health summary labels and a first-run handoff into Planning Wizard. Those labels and visible state semantics are GUI-related even though the payload is shared contract data.
items.impact: Readiness labels can bypass GUI truth, localization, and accessibility review.

evidence.exact_quote: `health_summary_state` uses canonical machine values such as `ready`, `needs_setup`, `needs_attention`, and `could_not_connect`, with GUI labels `Ready`, `Needs setup`, `Needs attention`, and `Could not connect`.

items.title: Onboarding booleans and health state lack invalid-combination rules
items.statement: The contract allows setup_completed and setup_skipped to coexist but does not define whether both true is valid, how counts and free_models_reviewed affect readiness, precedence among owner facts, freshness, versioning, or transition/recovery rules after later provider changes.
items.impact: Planning Wizard and Health can render conflicting readiness from the same payload or retain stale first-run state indefinitely.

evidence.exact_quote: The minimum fields are `setup_completed`, `setup_skipped`, `connected_provider_count`, `provider_warning_count`, `free_models_reviewed`, and `health_summary_state`.

items.title: WebSocket admission is fail-closed before initialize
items.statement: CV-306 explicitly rejects remote or tunneled WebSocket initialization until auth, Origin, CSRF, runtime id, and permission scope pass, and limits receipts to redacted reason codes and secret references.
items.impact: Prevents an unauthenticated session from reaching runtime initialization and avoids raw credential logging.

evidence.exact_quote: WSAuthSession records auth_scheme, credential_ref, origin, csrf_token_hash, runtime_id, tunnel_id, permission_snapshot_id, expires_at_ms, and redacted_receipt_ref before any remote initialize is admitted.

items.title: WebSocket auth session omits transport, replay, and revocation semantics
items.statement: Configured auth is not an exact scheme contract. CV-306 does not define TLS requirements, Origin allowlist matching, CSRF issuance/binding, nonce or replay protection, credential rotation, session revocation, tunnel binding, runtime-id proof, clock skew, or what closes already-open sockets when permissions change.
items.impact: A token or session can be replayed, remain active after revocation, or be admitted under inconsistent origin/tunnel rules.

evidence.exact_quote: Remote/tunnel WS requires configured auth; wrong Origin/CSRF/runtime id is rejected before initialize; security receipts are visible and redacted.

items.title: Acknowledgement can be misread as readiness recovery
items.statement: CV-307 says unavailable or degraded surfaces block model-visible tool use until recovery is acknowledged. Acknowledging a failure is not proof that the surface is recovered, so the wording permits tool exposure without a new successful roundtrip probe.
items.impact: The model may receive a callable tool that remains unavailable or miswired after the user merely acknowledges the warning.

evidence.exact_quote: Readiness status values are ready, degraded, unavailable, disabled_by_policy, auth_required, restart_required, and namespace_mismatch; unavailable or degraded surfaces block model-visible tool use until recovery is acknowledged.

items.title: Runtime readiness probes lack freshness, timeout, and aggregate semantics
items.statement: The record has last_probe_at_ms but no TTL, timeout, retry budget, probe id/generation, idempotency, aggregate readiness rule, restart invalidation, network transition handling, or race rule when UI-visible and model-visible change during a probe.
items.impact: Stale readiness can survive restart or network loss, and concurrent probes can overwrite newer failure state.

evidence.exact_quote: RuntimeSurfaceReadinessProbe records surface_id, surface_kind, configured_enabled, process_or_port_ref, injection_state, model_visible, ui_visible, roundtrip_state, last_probe_at_ms, failure_reason_code, and recovery_command_ref.

items.title: Prompt admission idempotency collision and execution race behavior are undefined
items.statement: CV-308 defines states and replay by idempotency_key plus prompt_hash but does not say what happens when the same key arrives with a different hash, how client_sequence is scoped and ordered, who atomically binds execution_ref, or how expiry/cancellation races execution_bound.
items.impact: A prompt can execute twice, the wrong prompt can be treated as a duplicate, or cancellation can report success after execution begins.

evidence.exact_quote: Admission states are queued, admitted, duplicate_ignored, rejected, expired, cancelled_before_execution, and execution_bound; replay uses idempotency_key plus prompt_hash to avoid duplicate execution.

items.title: Prompt admission lacks privacy, size, retention, and rejection detail boundaries
items.statement: prompt_hash and stored prompt auditability are introduced without a canonical hash algorithm/salt policy, payload size limit, retention/deletion rule, tenant scope, redaction profile, abuse/rate limit, or exact rejection_reason_code registry.
items.impact: Sensitive prompts can be retained or correlated indefinitely, and admission can be exhausted with oversized or high-rate submissions.

evidence.exact_quote: SessionPromptAdmission events include admission_id, thread_id, prompt_id, prompt_hash, client_sequence, idempotency_key, submitted_at_ms, admitted_at_ms, admission_state, duplicate_of?, execution_ref?, and rejection_reason_code?.

items.title: EventRecord is explicitly narrow and legacy type is compatibility-only
items.statement: CV-309 defines one canonical persisted envelope, requires event_type normalization, forbids a second persisted type field and raw secrets, and explicitly refuses to treat envelope materialization as broad runtime completion.
items.impact: Prevents duplicate event discriminators and false closure of unrelated payload, lifecycle, GUI, or security work.

evidence.exact_quote: Contracts_V0 owns the canonical persisted EventRecord envelope for schema_id pm.event.v0 and schema_version 1.0.0 through Plans/event_record.schema.json.

items.title: EventRecord cross-field invariants are not established by this source unit
items.statement: CV-309 names identity, timestamp, sequence, idempotency, payload, redaction, replay, and migration fields but does not state optionality by event type, payload versus payload_ref exclusivity, sequence scope, timestamp ordering, idempotency uniqueness scope, or replay-policy semantics. A referenced schema may close some shape questions, but behavioral invariants remain unverified in this capsule.
items.impact: Structurally valid events can still be ambiguous, non-replayable, or contradictory across tenants and streams.

evidence.exact_quote: The envelope requires schema_id, schema_version, event_id, canonical event_type, project/thread/run/node/attempt identity fields, actor and requested/effective account refs, occurred/observed/persisted timestamps, monotonic sequence fields, correlation and causation ids, idempotency_key, payload_schema_id, payload and payload_ref dispatch fields, redaction_profile, replay_policy, and closed migration metadata.

systemic_patterns: Many units enumerate fields or obligations without closed schemas, legal state transitions, concurrency rules, or executable negative oracles.
Privileged boundaries are named more often than their freshness, revocation, idempotency, replay, and crash-recovery semantics are defined.
Several shared contract units are marked gui_related false despite directly governing user-visible labels, guided actions, inline visuals, and GUI state truth.
External-network and derived-content paths have strong redaction intent but incomplete SSRF, prompt-injection, authenticity, and lifecycle controls.
Cross-document pointers may contain additional shape detail, but this capsule cannot verify those seams; claims tied only to referenced schemas remain explicit unknowns rather than assumed closure.
highest_risk_seams: Planning activation commit, outbox, queue, cancellation, and crash recovery
Free Models import authenticity and activation TOCTOU
Privileged container host command replay and lease freshness
Remote WebSocket session replay, revocation, and transport security
Runtime readiness acknowledgement versus successful re-probe
Prompt admission idempotency collision and cancellation/execution races
